title: Test harness: MLX thread-local stream breaks shared cargo test
description: MLX's default stream is bound to the thread that calls init_mlx (OnceLock), but the test harness runs across a thread pool, so MLX-op tests (test_snake_activation, qmm_bench::*) hit 'no Stream(gpu,0) in current thread' unless run alone. Currently marked #[ignore]; run with --ignored --test-threads=1. Proper fix: a test helper that ensures the default stream is set on the current thread (or make default_stream() lazily bind per-thread), so these run in the normal suite. Low priority — worker correctness is covered by the benchmark+ASR integration path.

title: Worker requests get slower after the first synthesis
description:
Measured 2026-07-26 on M4 Max, MLX 6-bit 0.6B Base, one persistent 'spqx serve' worker, same text and reference each time (snake, 14.5s ref): run1 920ms/TTFA 97ms, run2 1048/123, run3 1989/161, run4 1534/239, run5 1163/161, run6 1229/140. The worker's own 'generated' JSON confirms it, so it is not a client measurement artifact: the FIRST request in a warm worker is the fastest, and later ones degrade by up to 2x with TTFA drifting 97ms -> 239ms.

This makes the persistent path SLOWER than one-shot 'spqx say' (0.195 engine RTF), which defeats the point of the worker and is what foxline uses for interactive latency.

Prime suspect: clear_mlx_cache() (worker.rs:565) runs after every speak, calling mlx_clear_cache() and throwing away MLX's buffer cache so each request re-allocates. Compare against qwentts.cpp, whose warm server is stable across requests. Next step: measure with the clear removed / made periodic, and check whether MLX cache limits (mlx_set_cache_limit) are a better lever than clearing outright.

Six-voice medians for the same setup were 0.325-0.439 RTF versus 0.195 cold engine-only. Raw data: ~/voice-tests/spqx-candle-mgs-2026-07-26/results/mlx-warm/.
close_reason:
NOT REPRODUCIBLE — measurement contamination, not a bug. Re-tested 2026-07-26 on an idle machine with 10 consecutive requests to one warm worker, on both the installed binary (sha 465981da) and a fresh build of the current tree (sha e4f5b7ee): wall 801-911ms, TTFA 94-112ms, RTF 0.194-0.201, drift 1.00x. No degradation on either.

The original degrading series (920/1048/1989/1534/1163/1229ms, TTFA 97->239ms) was measured immediately after a qwentts.cpp Metal benchmark loop had been hammering the GPU, so the worker was competing for Metal and a hot machine. clear_mlx_cache() (worker.rs:565) is exonerated — left as is.

Correct warm MLX baseline: ~0.195 RTF, ~95ms TTFA, stable across requests. The earlier 0.374 six-voice warm figure was contaminated by the same cause and has been corrected in wiki projects/codec-mgs-tts-backends.md.

Lesson for future runs: leave an idle gap between GPU benchmark suites, and always check drift over >=10 requests before believing a warm number.

title: Build reproducibility: pin MLX by commit, consider vendoring
description: MLX core is FetchContent'd by mlx-c's CMake at tag v0.31.2 — clean builds need network and trust the tag not to move. Options when packaging (spqx v0.1): pin by commit hash instead of tag in byteowlz/mlx-c, cache/vendor the MLX source, or ship prebuilt lib+metallib artifacts so end users never build MLX at all (preferred; aligns with the packaged-metallib roadmap item). Remember the build.rs source patch (metal4.0 misfire) applies to the fetched tree and must survive whatever pinning strategy is chosen.

title: Durable metal4.0 JIT fix in build.rs
description: MLX get_metal_version() selects -std=metal4.0 behind __builtin_available(macOS 26) which misfires on macOS 15 + Xcode 26 and aborts runtime kernel JIT. build.rs now patches the FetchContent'd mlx-src after the first cmake build and rebuilds (idempotent, survives cargo clean). Candidate for upstream PR to ml-explore/mlx (proper fix: verify compiler support, not just OS version).
close_reason: Landed in 308117a; verified end-to-end by fresh release build + benchmark run (no metal4.0 JIT abort).

title: Upstream PRs to badlogic/qwen3_tts_rs
description: Upstream candidates to badlogic once validated: (1) metal4.0 build.rs patch, (2) IclPromptCache/IclSession API, (3) first-chunk gate + warm vocoder state, (4) python-parity sampling (penalty 1.5 unique-set, special-token suppression, EOS top-k exemption), (5) RoPE table slicing, (6) mask dtype fixes, (7) IMPORTANT: mlx-c qmm chunking is a workaround for HIS toolchain's miscompiled metallib, not an MLX bug — byteowlz/mlx-c spqx branch makes it opt-in with a numerical parity test; tell him CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET + a working metal toolchain fix the root cause. (8) effective_max_tokens cap from text length (python has it; cheap runaway insurance — not yet ported).

title: ICL prompt cache: precompute reference prompt per session
description: TTFA scaled with reference length (~9.6ms/ref-second) because build_input_embeddings_with_icl rebuilt the reference prompt per request: ~16 tiny MLX ops per ref codec frame. Added IclPromptCache + IclSession (inference.rs): phases 1/2/4 + ref-text embeddings computed once in prepare_icl_session at worker startup; per-request only synthesis tokens are embedded. Worker uses generate_with_icl_session_streaming. Pending: benchmark vs python-mlx baseline (foxline benchmarks/tts_ab_bench.py), listening check for regression, upstream PR.
close_reason: Landed in 1a8713a. Median TTFA 228->~210ms across 7 MGS voices; output correctness confirmed by benchmark run. Remaining ref-length scaling is the prefill forward — spqx-vsnm.

title: Port effective_max_tokens cap from mlx_audio
description: python caps generation at min(max_tokens, max(75, text_token_count * 6)) — cheap insurance turning any runaway from 122s at the 1536-frame cap into a few seconds. Port into generate_with_icl_session_streaming (tokenized synth text length is available there).
close_reason: Landed in generate_with_icl_session_streaming (the worker path). Benchmark sanity: normal utterances unaffected (miller short 3.61s, long 16.21s audio).

title: spqx v0.1: standalone CLI + OpenAI-compatible API service
description:
APPROVED 2026-07-08. One installable spqx binary as the human/agent interface; the flag-only worker binary stays untouched as foxline's latency path (never HTTP for the gateway). House conventions per templates-repo + lst + mmry/trx analysis: hand-rolled config (NO config crate, NO dirs crate — zero-dep base_dir XDG helper), schemars draft-07 schema auto-written with # @schema header, clap derive with flattened global CommonOpts, config show|path|paths|schema|reset family, completions, LOGGING.md-conformant output. Borrow from kokorox (koko): ChannelSource rodio streaming playback, quote/ordinal/decimal-aware sentence segmentation, voices UX, pipe mode.

ZERO-CONFIG FIRST RUN (corrected 2026-07-09): the earlier 'CustomVoice preset speakers' plan is DROPPED — CustomVoice can't voice-clone and the Base model has no presets. Instead ship ~4 embedded reference voices (cloned from Kokoro/koko outputs, one per af_/am_/bf_/bm_ quadrant, ~1.6MB FLAC, in spqx-cli only) so 'say' works offline with zero downloads (kazg.11). More voices via 'spqx voices get' from configurable HF voice libraries (kazg.11); users can record their own via 'spqx voices record' with a prompted per-language sentence and no ASR needed (kazg.12). Cloned voices live in the named XDG registry (also the future resolution target for foxline personas and the API voice param). read2me is a downstream consumer. Phases tracked as child tasks with dependencies.

title: Workspace restructure: spqx-core + spqx-cli
description: Convert to a cargo workspace: crates/spqx-core (the current engine lib — rename crate qwen3-tts-rs to spqx-core, keep module structure; existing bins tts/voice_clone/api_server/trace_* stay wired for now) and crates/spqx-cli (new, bin name 'spqx'). spqx-tts-worker + pibot-tts-worker alias keep building unchanged from the same worker source — flag-only, zero config file, this is foxline's latency path and must not grow a config dependency. Update foxline resolver expectations only if binary output paths change (target/release/ stays the same for workspace builds). Errors: thiserror in core (exists as error.rs), anyhow in cli. Absorbs part of spqx-tx9r (crate rename).
close_reason: Done in ee6d1a8: cargo workspace, crates/spqx-core (crate renamed to spqx-core / lib spqx_core) + crates/spqx-cli scaffold. Worker bins still build from spqx-core at the same target/release path, so foxline's resolver needs no change (benchmark-verified). build.rs now links compiler-rt for MLX's __builtin_available guard.

title: spqx ref: reference hygiene toolchain
description: The differentiator — productize the pipeline that fixed mei_ling and nastasha: ref check <wav> (duration bounds 6-12s, isolated spike-over-silence scan, trailing-transient/tail analysis, format/sample-rate report), ref trim <wav> --start/--end or --auto (sentence-boundary cut using word timestamps; needs an ASR provider — subprocess out to a configured command, e.g. uv run mlx-whisper, config [asr] command; no hard whisper dependency in the binary), ref verify <voice> (generate a fixed test utterance set, optionally ASR the output and assert first words present; emit --json report). Wire 'voices add --check' to run check automatically. Guidelines source: foxline fxl-6ybb + spqx README Voice references section.

title: spqx voices get: embedded defaults + configurable HF voice libraries
description: Corrects the epic's zero-config story: CustomVoice presets can't clone and the Base model has no presets, so zero-config speech instead ships a handful of embedded reference voices cloned from Kokoro (koko) outputs. (1) EMBED ~4 default references (one per af_/am_/bf_/bm_ quadrant, ~1.6MB FLAC) in the spqx-cli crate only (NOT spqx-core, so the foxline worker stays lean) via include_bytes!; on first run seed them into the registry (or resolve them virtually) so 'spqx say' generates speech offline with zero downloads. Set one as config voice.default. (2) 'spqx voices get <name>' pulls individual voices on demand into the registry. (3) Config gains a list of voice LIBRARIES (HF dataset repos); ship one byteowlz default library pre-configured; users append their own HF libraries; 'voices get' resolves a name across configured libraries, downloads reference.wav+reference.txt into the registry (respect HF_HOME, mirror models pull/kazg.6 resolution). (4) 'voices list' shows embedded + registry + available-in-libraries. Source library content: the 27 Kokoro singles + 15 renamed blends generated in voice-auditions/ (shared _transcript.txt is the ICL transcript). Voice pack lives as a byteowlz HF dataset (e.g. byteowlz/spqx-voices).

title: spqx voices record: prompted-read (no ASR) or transcribe -> add reference
description:
One-step capture of a new cloned voice. TWO modes:

MODE A - PROMPTED READ (default, no ASR): 'spqx voices record <name> [--lang xx]' displays a fixed reference sentence in the chosen language and the user reads it aloud. Because we supplied the text, the transcript is already known -> NO transcription step, no ASR dependency on the common path. We ship the reference sentence in multiple languages (a small bundled table: lang -> sentence, each designed for ICL hygiene: phonetically varied, ~8-10s when read at a natural pace, sentence-boundary). Capture mic (press-enter-to-stop or --seconds N), run ref check (kazg.10), then 'voices add' with the known transcript. This is the easy path and works offline with zero extra tools.

MODE B - FREE / EXISTING AUDIO (ASR fallback): '--transcribe' or passing a pre-recorded --file records/accepts arbitrary speech and transcribes by shelling out to a CONFIGURABLE backend (reuse kazg.10 [asr] config: ears / trscrb / whisper CLI / parakeet CLI; no hard ASR dep in the binary). For voices where we don't control the script.

Capture backend: cpal or shell out to sox/ffmpeg/arecord (configured record command); pick simplest cross-platform path.

Primary use case: record yourself in different languages so the clone carries your accent (speak German -> English output keeps the German accent). LANGUAGE MANAGEMENT via naming prefixes only for now: extend the af_/am_ scheme with a language segment, e.g. de_m_snake / en_f_meiling; document the convention, no language subsystem. The bundled per-language reference sentences double as the prompts for Mode A.

Deps: Mode A depends only on kazg.5 (registry) + kazg.10 ref check (optional). Mode B additionally needs kazg.10 [asr] config.

title: CLI plumbing: lean config, XDG paths, schema, completions
description: House pattern WITHOUT the config and dirs crates. (1) Zero-dep XDG: copy base_dir(xdg_env, unix_fallback, windows_env) helper from templates-repo/rust-cli (config/data/state/cache dirs under <dir>/spqx). (2) Config: serde structs with per-section Default impls + #[serde(default)], plain toml::from_str; precedence = defaults -> ~/.config/spqx/config.toml -> --config flag or SPQX_CONFIG env (path override only; NO generic env-override matrix — flags cover per-run tweaks). Auto-write default config on first run with '# @schema ./config.schema.json' header AND write config.schema.json alongside (schemars draft-07, $id -> byteowlz/schemas). (3) Sections: [model] (id, path override, quantization), [voice] (default voice name or preset speaker), [audio] (sample_rate, output_dir), [sampling] (temperature, top_k), [playback] (enabled, device later), [api] (ip, port), [paths] (voices_dir, models_dir overrides). (4) Subcommands: config show|path|paths|schema|reset (honoring --json), completions <shell> via clap_complete. (5) Global CommonOpts flattened: --config, --json, -q, -v (count), --debug, --no-color/--color, --yes. (6) Logging per templates-repo LOGGING.md: env_logger, NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR respected, JSON Lines when piped is a later nicety.
close_reason: Done in ee6d1a8: lean config (no config/dirs crate) — paths.rs zero-dep XDG, config.rs plain-TOML with per-section defaults + schema auto-write, main.rs clap derive with global CommonOpts, config show|path|paths|schema|reset, completions. Verified: config paths/show/schema/reset and completions all work; ~/.config/spqx/{config.toml,config.schema.json} written on first run.

title: spqx say: synthesize with live playback
description: spqx say [TEXT] (or stdin when '-' / no arg + piped). Streams synthesis through the existing session API (prepare_icl_session / generate_with_icl_session_streaming for cloned voices; CustomVoice path with preset speakers for zero-setup). Live playback via rodio using kokorox's ChannelSource pattern (kokorox/koko/src/main.rs:28-77): mpsc<Vec<f32>> -> Source<i16>, keep OutputStream alive, sink.append. Flags: --voice <registry-name|preset> (default from config), --out <wav> (write while playing), --no-play, --language, --speed, --seed, --json (emit {ttfa_ms, audio_s, rtf, wav_path} for agents — mirrors worker stderr events). First run with no model: auto-resolve HF cache, offer pull (see models task). Reuses worker's output-cleanup gates (gate_leading_nonspeech lives in worker bin — move to spqx-core so CLI and worker share it).
close_reason: Done in 84aa9fc: spqx say drives the ICL session path with live-playback (rodio ChannelSource) + --out WAV + --json. Reference from --ref-audio/--ref-text(-file) or --voice registry lookup. Shared gate_leading_nonspeech moved to spqx_core::postprocess. Engine println redirected stdout->stderr so --json stays clean (verified single-line valid JSON). Measured: campbell clone 91-96ms TTFA RTF ~0.19; stdin path works; ASR-confirmed audio. FOLLOW-UP not blocking: (1) live playback verified to compile/not-crash but needs on-device ear check; (2) default voice 'aiden' is a CustomVoice preset needing the CustomVoice model — presets unwired, use --ref-audio or registry until then.

title: spqx read: long-form file/stdin reading
description: spqx read FILE|- : long-form text -> continuous speech. Sentence segmentation adapted from kokorox (kokorox/src/tts/segmentation.rs — quote-depth tracking, ordinals, decimals, abbreviations; UTF-8 safe) feeding sentence-sized synth requests into one warm session (ICL prompt cache makes per-sentence cost ~TTFA only). Progress line (sentences done/total, elapsed, RTF; --no-progress). Formats: plain text + markdown (strip formatting to speakable prose — reuse ideas from foxline ws.rs normalize_tts_text; full verbalization of times/numbers is foxline fxl-ma47.4, coordinate not duplicate). --out concatenated wav, --from-sentence N resume. PDFs/HTML explicitly out of scope (read2me territory).

title: spqx voices: named voice registry
description: Registry at ~/.local/share/spqx/voices/<name>/ with reference.wav, reference.txt, voice.toml (display name, language hint, notes, source). Subcommands: voices list (table; --json), voices add <name> --ref-audio --ref-text[-file] (validates: duration 6-12s warn outside, spike-over-silence scan, tail check — the cheap parts of ref hygiene inline), voices show <name>, voices rm <name>. Preset speakers (CustomVoice model: serena/vivian/uncle_fu/ryan/aiden/ono_anna/sohee/eric/dylan) listed alongside registry entries. This registry is the future resolution target for the API voice param and optionally foxline personas.
close_reason: Done in d8fbb5c: voices list|add|show|rm. Registry at <voices_dir>/<name>/ (reference.wav 24kHz mono + reference.txt + voice.toml). add runs cheap hygiene (duration bounds + click scan) as warnings — verified it flags campbell's real 12.7s + click. 'say --voice <name>' resolves the registry; end-to-end add->say->rm verified, ASR-clean at 90ms TTFA. Presets listed for discoverability (need CustomVoice model, unwired).

title: spqx models: pull/list/path
description: models list (known Qwen3-TTS MLX ids + which are in HF cache), models pull <id> (download via hf_hub-style resolution into HF cache; respect HF_HOME), models path <id> (print snapshot dir — port hf_snapshot_path from foxline ws.rs into spqx-core so both share it). Default model from config [model]. Needed for the zero-config first-run story in 'say'.

title: spqx serve: worker protocol as a subcommand
description: spqx serve = the binary worker protocol (9-byte frames on stdin/stdout) behind the unified CLI, sharing the config layer for defaults (model, sampling) while every flag still overrides — the standalone spqx-tts-worker binary REMAINS flag-only and config-free for foxline/PiBot compatibility; serve is the same worker loop compiled into the cli. Extract the worker loop from src/bin/worker.rs into spqx-core so bin and subcommand share one implementation (incl. gate_leading_nonspeech, PcmStreamer).
close_reason: Done: worker loop extracted to spqx_core::worker (WorkerConfig-parameterized); bin/worker.rs reduced to a clap shell, spqx serve added sharing the same run_stdio. Standalone worker unchanged in behavior (89-91ms benchmark), spqx serve verified over the frame protocol (READY 0.6s, 93ms TTFA). Unblocks kazg.8 (api) and kazg.9 (packaging).

title: spqx api: OpenAI-compatible HTTP service
description: spqx api --ip --port (defaults from config [api]). Migrate/harden the existing api_server bin: POST /v1/audio/speech (input, voice, response_format wav|pcm first, mp3 via existing mp3lame dep later, speed), GET /v1/audio/voices (registry + presets, kokorox-openai has the reference shape incl. /voices/detailed). Chunked/streaming response while synthesis runs. voice param resolves through the voices registry. One warm session per voice with LRU eviction (0.3s model load makes cold misses cheap). Explicit non-goals: auth/multi-tenant; foxline never uses this path.

title: Packaging: bespoke release.yml + byt checksums/publish handoff (mlx only)
description:
Done (this pass): .github/workflows/release.yml replaced (the old one was
pre-rename cruft — retired bin names tts/voice_clone/api_server, Python HF
tokenizer download, full libtorch bundling for tch). New workflow:
build-macos (native cargo, --no-default-features --features mlx, aarch64-apple-darwin)
stages spqx + spqx-tts-worker into the ADR-0021 tarball shape
(spqx-v{ver}-{triple}/bin/), then a publish job in the byt container runs
`byt release checksums` + `byt release publish` only — byt's `release build`
is NOT used (no per-target feature-flag support, can't express mlx-vs-tch as
mutually exclusive per-platform binaries). Minimal byt.release.toml
([release] name/lang only) exists just so those two subcommands resolve
version/name; `byt release build`/`run` will misbehave here (silently tries
the tch-backend default) — don't use them.

Corrected assumption: no metallib sidecar needed. Verified empirically —
copied spqx-tts-worker alone into an empty dir, ran it, got "MLX backend
initialized (Metal GPU)" with zero other files present. build.rs statically
links mlxc/mlx and the Metal JIT patches its language-version check at build
time (no external .metallib load path in source, confirmed via grep). The
metallib bundling in the old release.yml was a leftover workaround from
before that build.rs fix landed.

Shipped and verified green end-to-end: v0.3.0 tag -> release published with
spqx-v0.3.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz (bin/{spqx,spqx-tts-worker} + LICENSE
+ README.md) + checksums.txt, matching ADR-0021 exactly. Two CI bugs found
and fixed en route:
1. macos-14's stock clang can't compile MLX's __fp16 SIMD template code
   (backend/cpu/simd/accelerate_simd.h) - unrelated to spqx's own code, a
   toolchain-version issue. Fixed by switching runs-on to macos-latest.
2. GITHUB_REF_NAME is a reserved GitHub Actions env var and is silently
   ignored when set via env: in a step (matches the wiki's documented
   "vmaster" gotcha) - byt release publish read the branch name (main)
   instead of the tag and published a bogus "vmain" release. Fixed by
   passing --tag explicitly to byt release publish instead of relying on
   env var propagation. Bad vmain release+tag deleted, v0.3.0 re-cut and
   verified.

Deferred (unchanged): tch/CUDA distribution until spqx-srtg (candle backend)
lands. Homebrew/AUR publishing not wired (byt.release.toml has no
[release.homebrew]/[release.aur] section) - only relevant once spqx needs to
be installable outside foxline. foxline-side installer/resolver to
auto-fetch this release asset (ahead of the sibling-repo/PATH fallback in
resolve_rust_tts_worker) not started - not yet requested as an active task.
close_reason: v0.3.0 released green end-to-end, artifact shape verified against ADR-0021

title: First-chunk fade-in to kill utterance-start pop
description: spqx-nspf First-chunk fade-in to kill utterance-start pop
close_reason: Output-side pops solved: warm vocoder state + click gate with density-based onset, plosive-preserving backward walk, and 50ms duration cap on the zeroer (each constraint added after an ear-caught regression: clamping ate onsets, blanket zeroing ate plosives, run-length test protected 20ms bursts, uncapped zeroer ate soft words). SPQX_NO_GATE debug bypass + mlx-whisper ASR loop used to separate gate bugs from model behavior. Remaining clicks-on-speech are reference/voice-driven (engine-independent) — foxline asset work.

title: GGML backend: quantized CUDA/CPU inference via qwentts.cpp
description:
SUPERSEDES THE CANDLE PLAN (decided 2026-07-26 after benchmarking). Fill the non-Apple slot with ServeurpersoCom/qwentts.cpp (MIT, GGML) instead of a candle port. Same goal as before: quantized inference on CUDA/CPU without libtorch's ~2GB runtime, single binary on Linux, Windows plausible; combined with MLX this makes spqx the cross-platform Qwen3-TTS engine.

WHY THE SWITCH — matched six-voice MGS ICL-cloning benchmark, 0.6B Base, seed 42 (raw data ~/voice-tests/spqx-candle-mgs-2026-07-26, wiki projects/codec-mgs-tts-backends.md):
- CUDA RTX 3070: qwentts Q8_0 0.435 cold / 0.149 WARM. TrevorS candle dense BF16 0.646 cold, no quantized path. At matched BF16 qwentts still wins (0.524 vs 0.646), so the engine matters more than the weight format.
- The warm persistent server is the biggest single win (0.44 -> 0.149), bigger than any quantization step.
- KevinKickass/chew-tts (native rust CUDA) ruled out: loads fine but every Base cloning request fails with CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE on the 3070/CUDA 13.3.
- Quality: Q8_0 is indistinguishable from MLX by ear; Q4_K_M slightly loses rhythm and saves memory, not time. Ship Q8_0.
- CPU: M4 Max 0.80 warm RTF (usable fallback), 4-vCPU VM 4.4 RTF (unusable, and that box has no BLAS).
- Apple Metal: does NOT replace MLX. Warm totals tie (MLX 0.374 vs Metal 0.384) and Metal wins TTFA hard (32ms vs 209ms) but its codec decode costs ~930ms vs 138ms on CUDA. Revisit only if that stage is optimized.

SCOPE: CUDA-first, CPU as honest fallback, Vulkan/ROCm come free from GGML. Do NOT add Metal — it would be a second Apple backend that buys nothing.

SEAM (see also the crate question): the engine boundary is whole-pipeline (text -> WAV), NOT the per-op tensor abstraction in spqx-core/src/tensor.rs where mlx/tch live. libqwen does its own tokenization, talker, code predictor and codec. So it plugs in behind synthesize_streaming, and that function should move from spqx-cli/src/engine.rs into spqx-core first, because worker.rs and api/ need the same path. Feature-gate as 'qwentts'.

INTEGRATION MODE — still open: (a) link libqwen (C ABI, qt_* symbols, qt_extract_voice_ref for in-process .spk/.rvq latents) for a self-contained binary, or (b) spawn its tts-server as a subprocess (no FFI, no compile-time CUDA, but we host a fat artifact and own version skew). Note upstream has NO releases/tags, so either way byteowlz builds and publishes the artifacts.

PERF NOTE: use pre-extracted .spk/.rvq reference latents (qwen-codec --talker, or qt_extract_voice_ref in-process). They remove the speaker encoder + codec encode from every synthesis and are what make the warm path fast.

BUILD GOTCHAS: Arch w/ GCC 16 needs -DCMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER=/usr/bin/g++-15 plus explicit -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES. Pre-converted GGUFs exist at Serveurperso/Qwen3-TTS-GGUF (talker + shared tokenizer load as two files), so no local conversion step.

The old candle survey (qwen_tts crate, Crane, TrevorS, darkautism) is kept in git history; TrevorS remains readable reference material for streaming idioms only.

title: Wire libqwen or tts-server as the GGML engine behind spqx-core
description: Was: evaluate qwen_tts crate vs crane-core. Superseded by the 2026-07-26 benchmark — the base is qwentts.cpp (MIT). Remaining work: (1) move synthesize_streaming from spqx-cli/src/engine.rs into spqx-core so worker.rs and api/ share it, (2) define the whole-pipeline engine seam there, (3) decide link-libqwen vs spawn-tts-server, (4) feature-gate as 'qwentts' and validate Q8_0 cloning quality against the MLX baseline on the MGS set.

title: Port streaming architecture onto the candle base
description: The MLX backend's shape, re-expressed in candle: IclSession prompt cache, generate_codes_streaming with chunked on_chunk callback, vocoder streaming state (causal conv/transformer state structs) with reference-tail warm state, python-parity code-0 sampling (unique-set penalty 1.5, special-token suppression, EOS top-k exemption — port the unit test), device-side predictor chaining (1 sync/frame).

title: GGUF quantization for the talker LM

title: Parity + performance validation vs MLX and python

title: Decode-loop RTF parity with python-mlx
description: STATUS (7e485fb, 74ab707, +parity commit): rust-mlx TTFA median 144ms p95 194ms RTF 0.20 load 0.3s vs python-mlx 120ms/171ms/0.22/2.3s — RTF now BEATS python; 0 runaways/49. Landed: bf16 activation stream, causal SDPA, device decode loop (1 sync/frame), python-parity code-0 sampling (unique-set penalty @1.5 ICL, special-token suppression, EOS top-k exemption; -1e9 not -inf to avoid NaN poisoning). PENDING: quality listening on regenerated wavs (sampling changed); remaining 24ms median TTFA = prefill rate (~0.35ms/pos vs python ~0.2) — candidates: qmm dispatch at M~300, prefill-timing eval sync removal, mx-compile-style step fusion.
close_reason: DONE — rust beats python on every metric: TTFA median 96ms vs 120ms (p95 152 vs 175), RTF 0.20 vs 0.22, load 0.3s vs 2.3s, 0 runaways/49. Root cause of the final gap: mlx-c fork's unconditional 16-row qmm chunking (workaround for a toolchain-miscompiled metallib; correct + 4-8x faster unchunked on a sound toolchain, guarded by a numerical parity test). Full trail: bf16 activation stream, causal SDPA + mask dtype, device decode loop, python-parity sampling, RoPE table slicing, full-batch qmm via byteowlz/mlx-c (spqx branch, chunking opt-in via MLX_C_CHUNKED_QMM). Upstream candidates tracked in spqx-hm38 (now incl. the mlx-c finding for badlogic).

title: Guard against silent long-generation failure (both engines)
description:
Long single generations fail SILENTLY on both engines: the caller gets a success result and a WAV whose tail is silence or garbage. Measured 2026-07-26, 0.6B Base, snake reference, one generation per input (no sentence splitting). Speech-end times confirmed by listening, not just RMS.

| input | MLX | qwentts Q8_0 |
|---|---|---|
| 76 words | 23s clean | 24s clean, EOS |
| 228 words | 68s clean | 69s clean, EOS |
| 380 words | 133s clean, EOS | 116s clean, EOS |
| 608 words | speech ENDS at 2:25, then 189s of noise floor; json still reports audio_s=334 | hard truncation at 163.84s (2048 frames), no EOS, cut mid-sentence |
| 1216 words | speech ENDS at 1:40, artifact burst 1:50-2:00, then 11 MINUTES of digital silence; json reports audio_s=668, rtf 0.29, exit 0 | same 163.84s truncation |

KEY INSIGHT: it is not a fixed duration ceiling, it is coherence collapse that arrives EARLIER the longer the input — 380 words finished cleanly at 133s, 1216 words died at 100s. So a duration-only guard is not sufficient.

THREE DISTINCT CEILINGS FOUND:
1. MLX has no hard cap; it runs to effective_max_codes = text_tokens*6 (inference.rs:3196) and pads with silence after the model stops speaking. Worst failure mode: looks successful.
2. qwentts --max-new defaults to 2048 frames = 163.84s -> silent truncation, no EOS flag surfaced to the caller.
3. qwentts KV cache is hard-capped at 4096 slots. Raising --max-new to 16384 does NOT extend it: FATAL 'decode would overflow cache (4097 > 4096)' at 3904 frames, NO output at all, 74s of work lost. Real ceiling ~3900 frames (~310s) minus prompt, and crossing it is fatal rather than graceful.

WANTED:
- Cap segment length so we never approach 2048 frames / the 4096-slot cache. spqx read (kazg.4) already segments; make the bound explicit and shared, not per-callsite.
- Treat 'generated frames == max' (no EOS) as an ERROR, not success — both engines can report it.
- Detect a trailing silent/degenerate tail and fail or trim rather than returning it. postprocess.rs already has gate_leading_nonspeech; the trailing case is the dangerous one.
- Surface EOS-reached in SynthStats and in the worker's 'generated' JSON so callers can tell a complete generation from a truncated one.
- For the GGML backend (spqx-srtg): set --max-new / max frames from the segment length and never let a request reach the cache limit, since that path is FATAL.

Audio evidence: /tmp/dur/out (mlx-s*.wav, qt-s*.wav); regenerate with the texts in /tmp/dur/*.txt.

title: Ship all GGML backends from one artifact (CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, SYCL, CPU variants)
description:
Child of spqx-srtg. Goal: one Linux artifact that runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel or plain CPU, chosen at runtime — not one build per vendor.

GOOD NEWS: this is mostly PACKAGING, not code. qwentts.cpp already does the hard part (src/backend.h):
- backend_init() calls ggml_backend_load_all() once, so with -DGGML_BACKEND_DL=ON every backend is a sideloaded shared lib discovered at runtime.
- Default selection is ggml_backend_init_best().
- Override is the GGML_BACKEND env var, matching ggml device names: CUDA0, Vulkan0, CPU, BLAS (ggml_backend_init_by_name).
- Upstream buildall.sh already ships the exact recipe: -DGGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_VULKAN=ON -DGGML_BACKEND_DL=ON.

WORK:
1. Build matrix in the byteowlz release pipeline: linux-x86_64 with CPU_ALL_VARIANTS + CUDA + Vulkan (+ ROCm/SYCL once there is hardware to test on), macOS with Metal, and publish the ggml backend .so/.dylib set alongside the binary. Upstream has no releases/tags, so we build and publish regardless.
2. Backend resolution in spqx: config [engine] backend = auto|cuda|vulkan|rocm|cpu plus a --backend flag, mapped onto ggml device names. auto = ggml_backend_init_best().
3. If we LINK libqwen: qt_init_params has no backend field, only the GGML_BACKEND env var, so either setenv before qt_init (ugly but works) or upstream a params field — MIT, upstream takes PRs. If we SPAWN tts-server, pass it through the child env, which is clean.
4. Report the resolved device in spqx doctor / --json output; enumerate available devices for diagnostics (backend.h already builds that list on failure).
5. Per-backend validation on the MGS fixture: identical audio (seeded), plus RTF/TTFA/VRAM per backend. Do NOT assume a backend works because it compiles — chew-tts compiled and loaded fine and still failed every clone call.

STATUS OF VALIDATION: CUDA validated (0.149 warm RTF, RTX 3070). Metal validated but rejected for Apple (MLX is 2.2x faster warm). CPU validated on both M4 Max (0.80 warm, usable) and a 4-vCPU VM (4.6, unusable). Vulkan NOT yet validated — archvm has the ICD loader, shaderc and glslang but is missing vulkan-headers, so the build could not be configured. ROCm and SYCL have no hardware here.

RISK: binary size and the backend .so set grow a lot with CUDA included; consider shipping backends as a separate optional download resolved on first run.

VALIDATION POLICY (decided 2026-07-26): do NOT gate the release on benchmarking every backend. GGML 'supports' a backend at the op level, which does not mean the pipeline is fast or correct there — Metal compiled and ran fine yet its codec decode costs ~1050ms vs 138ms on CUDA, and missing ops can silently fall back to CPU. So: enable every backend GGML offers, benchmark only the paths we actively recommend (CUDA, CPU, MLX on Apple), and ship 'spqx doctor --backend <name>' which synthesizes a seeded utterance and reports the resolved ggml device plus RTF/TTFA. Validation then happens on the user's hardware instead of ours.

AMD: Vulkan is the default AMD path (RADV, plus Intel ANV and ARM Mali for free, no ROCm stack required). ROCm/HIP is faster on supported cards but has a narrow support matrix and a heavy runtime, so it stays an opt-in addition gated on having an AMD box to validate against. Linux artifact therefore carries CUDA + Vulkan + CPU_ALL_VARIANTS, which covers essentially any GPU spqx would run on.
